verses.text: This is how the land of Canaan was shared out among the Israelites. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the family groups of the tribes divided it among them.
The land for the nine and a half tribes was given out by drawing lots, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Moses had already given the two and a half tribes their land east of the Jordan, but he gave the Levites no land among them.
Joseph's descendants had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites received no share of the land, only towns to live in, with fields around them for their animals and belongings.
So the Israelites divided the land, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh Barnea about you and me.
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land. I brought back an honest report, just as I believed it.
But the others who went with me made the people's hearts melt with fear. I, however, followed the LORD my God with all my heart.
So on that day Moses swore to me, 'The land you walked on will belong to you and your children forever, because you followed the LORD my God with all your heart.'
Now look, the LORD has kept me alive for forty-five years, just as he promised, since the time he said this to Moses, while Israel wandered in the desert. Today I am eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. I am just as able to go out to battle now as I was then.
So give me this hill country the LORD promised me that day. You heard then that the Anakites were there, with large walled cities. But with the LORD's help I will drive them out, just as he said."
Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his own land.
So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite ever since, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakites. Then the land had rest from war.
